name: the-loading-ring-reads-at-a-glance
description: The ring around a loading row was reported as too faint to find without zooming into a screenshot. It now carries the favicon's hue moved toward white on a dark row or toward black on a light one, far enough to clear 3:1, and its stroke went from 2px to 3px. Two phases on one fixture: space 'Dark' is tinted #12282E (the darkest surround preset) and space 'Light' #F0F4F8 (the lightest), each holding a page that spins for three seconds so the ring is reliably up when the reads happen. The contrast is computed in the sidebar from the CASCADED values - getComputedStyle's --ringb against the row AS PAINTED, which is the selected row's own background-color composited over --selbase. The wash is the whole point: a red icon graded against the bare tint reads 3.01:1 on #12282E and 1.12:1 on the row that tint actually paints, and only the focused row rings now, so the focused row's wash is always in the way. The mid-load frames are captured on both tints as well: the harness cannot key a region assertion to the ring band, because a row's y moves with every sidebar size change (row heights have already retargeted 38 coordinate scenarios once), so the frames are here for a measured read rather than a guessed rectangle.

actions.note: the fixture page spins for 3s, so this outlasts the first load
PHASE 1, mid-load: well inside the fixture's 3s spin

actions.expression: (() => { const el = document.querySelector('.row.loading, .fav.loading'); if (!el) { return 'no ring'; } const cs = getComputedStyle(el); const rgba = (raw) => { const s = (raw || '').trim(); const h = /^#([0-9a-fA-F]{6})$/.exec(s); if (h) { return [0, 2, 4].map((i) => parseInt(h[1].substr(i, 2), 16)).concat(1); } const m = /^rgba?\(([^)]*)\)/.exec(s); const n = m && m[1].match(/[0-9.]+/g); if (!n || n.length < 3) { return null; } return [Number(n[0]), Number(n[1]), Number(n[2]), n.length > 3 ? Number(n[3]) : 1]; }; const lin = (v) => { const c = v / 255; return c <= 0.03928 ? c / 12.92 : Math.pow((c + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4); }; const lum = (c) => 0.2126 * lin(c[0]) + 0.7152 * lin(c[1]) + 0.0722 * lin(c[2]); const ring = rgba(cs.getPropertyValue('--ringb')); const tint = rgba(cs.getPropertyValue('--selbase')); if (!ring || !tint) { return 'unreadable ring ' + cs.getPropertyValue('--ringb') + ' on ' + cs.getPropertyValue('--selbase'); } const wash = rgba(cs.backgroundColor); const ground = wash && wash[3] > 0 ? [0, 1, 2].map((i) => Math.round(tint[i] * (1 - wash[3]) + wash[i] * wash[3])) : tint.slice(0, 3); const a = lum(ring); const b = lum(ground); const ratio = (Math.max(a, b) + 0.05) / (Math.min(a, b) + 0.05); return ratio >= 3 ? 'clears 3:1' : 'faint ' + ratio.toFixed(2) + ' on ' + ground.join(','); })()

(() => { const el = document.querySelector('.loading > .brdr'); if (!el) { return 'no ring'; } const w = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el, '::before').paddingTop); return w >= 2 ? 'at least 2px' : 'thin ' + w; })()

actions.note: let the reload finish before the space switch

assertions.desc: THE MEASUREMENT, on the darkest tint: the ring the cascade resolves reads 3:1 or better against the row #12282E paints under the selected-row wash. 'no ring' means the reload never marked and nothing was measured; 'faint N' is the old build's answer.

Read off ::before rather than off the sheet. sidebar.css's brdr::before now reads --selring (2px) rather than a hardcoded 3px, unifying the sweep with the solid ring's own width so a load no longer grows the row by a pixel (commit d4f1cf08ae719) - which also meets the 'at least 2px' minimum.
gates the phase: the second read really happened on the light space (#F0F4F8), not on the dark one it started in. Normalised to a triple so a hex the model reformats still compares.
THE MEASUREMENT, on the lightest tint: the same ring darkened instead of lightened, still 3:1 or better against the washed row
